title: Pre-training evaluation-protocol amendment A2 (Issues 1-6)
status: PROPOSED -- awaiting approval; nothing run or evaluated

provenance.original_wording_unchanged: Spec v2 files (preregistered_success_criteria.json, closed_loop_evaluation.json, selector_design.json, final_feature_manifest.json) are unchanged; A2 supersedes the listed clauses for evaluation purposes only and does not rewrite them
provenance.spec_v2_and_A1_results_unchanged: Original Spec v2 NO-GO, original G1/X5/X7 FAIL and the A1 evaluation result are unchanged
provenance.preregistration_gap: The Spec v2 commitment to set the closed-loop usefulness threshold 'from the Phase-1 pilot (spread between P2 and P5) BEFORE Phase 3' was never completed: no P2/P5 closed-loop run exists in any record, and the original wording specifies no metric, mapping, statistic or rule for a non-positive spread. A2 closes that gap post hoc, before any P2/P5 run and before training.

common_conventions.lexicographic_key: key(a, s) = (future_T90, future_T100, future_unmet, future_hazard_unmet) of candidate a at state s from the frozen labels; smaller is better; compared as exact integer tuples (the frozen established order T90 -> T100 -> unmet -> hazard-edge unmet)
common_conventions.bootstrap: two-sided 95% percentile intervals, 2,000 resamples, resampling whole trajectories (for closed-loop runs: whole paired episodes, one per configuration)
common_conventions.seed_note: seeds are fixed identifiers for reproducibility, chosen before any run; they carry no substantive choice

1_closed_loop_usefulness.original: Safety: P4 strictly worse than P2 (label-free default) in <= 1% of paired episodes (upper CI). Usefulness: NO threshold is justified yet -- the minimum meaningful gain will be set from the Phase-1 pilot (spread between P2 and P5) BEFORE Phase 3 and appended here with its hash.
1_closed_loop_usefulness.problem: No P2/P5 pilot result exists; the wording fixes no metric, mapping, statistic, or rule for a small or non-positive spread.
1_closed_loop_usefulness.decision: M-C (user decision): metric = paired mean T100 difference; the spread decides assessability; the threshold is the frozen 0.5-tick meaningful-difference resolution; no fraction of the spread is used.

reference_run.configurations: the 240 discarded pilot configurations exactly as frozen in dataset_design.json -> phases.PHASE_1_PILOT.exact_specification: 8 layouts x t_h {none, 3, 5, 7, 9} x p {0.5, 0.7, 0.9} x 2; seeds 190000-190239 (unique per configuration); compliance generate_compliance_vector('AILX_v1|PILOT|<layout>', seed, p). Outside every TRAIN/VALIDATION/TEST split; no primary-test configuration used.
reference_run.episodes: full episodes from reset, no epsilon perturbation, common random numbers (identical configuration and compliance vector for P2 and P5)
reference_run.P2: label-free default action issued globally at every decision tick
reference_run.P5: at every decision tick of its own episode, every BASE2_298 candidate is rolled out with the frozen dataset rollout (run_ai_learning_pilot.rollout: candidate now, label-free continuation afterwards) and the candidate with the lexicographically smallest key is applied; ties: d(s) if tied-optimal, else the lowest candidate id
reference_run.per_episode_metric: T100 = compute_metrics(sim.evacuated).T100 (absolute, from t=0; MAX_STEPS if censored, censoring reported)
reference_run.record: the run's outputs and their SHA-256 are appended to A2 as the completion of the original commitment

1_closed_loop_usefulness.reference_gap: Delta = mean over the 240 configurations of (T100_P2 - T100_P5), point estimate; a 95% bootstrap CI is reported descriptively only
1_closed_loop_usefulness.feasibility_rule: Delta >= 0.5 tick: usefulness assessable. Delta < 0.5 tick: usefulness NOT ASSESSABLE; P4's gain reported descriptively, neither PASS nor FAIL.
1_closed_loop_usefulness.p4_endpoint: on the TEST_PRIMARY_JOINT configurations (960; closed-loop, no epsilon, common random numbers for P2 and P4): gain = mean over configurations of (T100_P2 - T100_P4)
1_closed_loop_usefulness.pass_rule: if assessable: PASS iff the lower bound of the two-sided 95% bootstrap CI of the gain (2,000 resamples over paired episodes, seed 5544101) >= 0.5 tick; the lower bound is the confirmatory statistic; no point-estimate-only rule
1_closed_loop_usefulness.interpretation: P2/P5 establishes whether the available closed-loop reference gap reaches the frozen 0.5-tick meaningful-difference resolution; P4 must show a statistically supported improvement of at least that size. P4 is not required to capture any fixed fraction of the P2->P5 gap.
1_closed_loop_usefulness.threshold_provenance: 0.5 tick = selector_design.json tolerances.delta_T100 ('T90/T100 are integer ticks, so a half tick separates distinct values'), reused as the episode-level meaningful-difference resolution by user decision M-C
1_closed_loop_usefulness.safety_unchanged: P4 strictly worse than P2 (label-free default) in <= 1% of paired episodes, upper 95% CI bound; independent of usefulness
1_closed_loop_usefulness.caveat: Delta is measured on pilot configurations (8 layouts, training-level t_h and p); P4 is evaluated on the primary test (6 main layouts, held-out t_h and p). The population difference is inherent to Option B and is recorded.

2_recommendation.original: Outcome-equivalence rate greater than d(s)'s own, CI excluding 0, on states where some candidate strictly beats d(s). Exact oracle-action match: diagnostic only.
2_recommendation.problem: On states where some candidate strictly beats d(s), d(s) is never oracle-equivalent, so its rate is 0 by construction and the criterion collapses to 'rate > 0'.
2_recommendation.unit_of_analysis: decision state (each test family separately; primary = TEST_PRIMARY_JOINT)
2_recommendation.improvable_state: state s with min_a key(a, s) < key(d(s), s) (strict, exact integer comparison)
2_recommendation.selector_success: evaluation-side outcome equivalence: key(selected(s), s) == min_a key(a, s)
2_recommendation.primary_metric: oracle-behavior capture rate = (# improvable states with selector success) / (# improvable states)

semantics_boundary.evaluation_side_outcome_equivalence: equality of the realized frozen target 4-vectors; used ONLY to score recommendations after the fact; never a selector input
semantics_boundary.observable_candidate_semantics: two candidates are observably identical in state s iff their assignments agree on every eligible zone whose waiting count in the 26 admissible features is > 0 (waiting_R1, waiting_R2, waiting_C1, waiting_R3, waiting_R4, waiting_C2, waiting_H_total); computable at decision time; used only for the secondary diagnostic below and never to remove candidates

reference_rates_reported.default: d(s)'s capture rate on improvable states (= 0 by construction; stated, not a competitor)
reference_rates_reported.random_candidate: expected capture of a uniformly random candidate = mean over improvable states of (# candidates with the oracle key / 298), computed from labels

secondary_diagnostics: T100 and unmet regret vs the oracle key
observable-semantic match: selected candidate observably identical to some oracle-optimal candidate

threshold.absolute_numeric_threshold: NOT DEFENSIBLE without an arbitrary choice: no numeric threshold exists in the preregistration, and the only stated anchor (the default's own rate) is 0 by construction. FLAGGED; not chosen.
threshold.proposed_least_arbitrary_criterion: comparative, mirroring the frozen prediction criterion ('lower than the best baseline, paired CI excluding 0'): the learned selector's capture rate must exceed the capture rate of the identical frozen selector driven by the best preregistered non-learning baseline predictor, with the paired state-level difference's 95% bootstrap CI (trajectory-clustered, 2,000 resamples, seed 5544102) lower bound > 0
threshold.best_baseline_rule: among the preregistered baselines able to provide conditional means and quantiles -- mean by candidate; mean by candidate x decision tick; exact-input lookup (falling back to candidate x tick when the input is unseen in TRAIN); 1-NN (ties averaged) -- the one with the lowest VALIDATION primary prediction loss (issue 3 convention); its quantiles are the empirical TRAIN quantiles of its own grouping; selected on VALIDATION only, before any test data is scored
threshold.excluded_baseline: default-outcome-as-prediction (it always selects d(s) and equals the default reference)
threshold.status: post-hoc pre-training proposal; requires explicit approval

3_prediction_loss_weighting.original: On the primary test, pinball loss (averaged over the three quantiles) on future_T100 and future_unmet is lower than the best baseline, with the paired-difference CI excluding 0; upper-quantile coverage within 0.9 +/- 0.05.
3_prediction_loss_weighting.problem: 91.7% of rows are behavioral duplicates and no weighting was specified.
3_prediction_loss_weighting.primary_convention: equal weight per candidate row for every primary prediction metric (pinball loss for quantiles 0.1/0.5/0.9 on future_T100 and future_unmet, and quantile coverage), for the model and every baseline alike
3_prediction_loss_weighting.equal_state_weight: every decision state has exactly 298 candidate rows (verified: 5,524,324 = 18,538 x 298), so equal row weight gives every decision state the same total weight, 298 rows
3_prediction_loss_weighting.paired_CI: difference in row-weighted loss between model and best baseline; bootstrap over trajectories (all rows of a resampled trajectory move together), 2,000 resamples, seed 5544104
3_prediction_loss_weighting.training_loss: the training objective also uses equal row weights; weighting by equivalence_class, hidden compliance or candidate frequency is prohibited
3_prediction_loss_weighting.secondary_diagnostics: behavior-level metrics (one row per realized-outcome class, or per observable-semantic class) may be reported; they never replace the primary metric
3_prediction_loss_weighting.T90_rows: rows with T90 reached before the decision (future_T90 = 0 for every candidate of the state) are kept; T90 is not a primary prediction metric

4_safety_denominator.original: Harmful-recommendation rate: upper 95% CI bound <= 1% of decisions in every test family. Derivation: ... the rule-of-three bound needs >= 300 independent deviating decisions ...
4_safety_denominator.problem: denominator ambiguous (all decisions vs deviating decisions); candidate rows must not count as independent decisions
4_safety_denominator.unit_of_analysis: decision state; exactly one selector recommendation per state
4_safety_denominator.eligible_state: every evaluation decision state of the family whose 298 candidate labels are all present and finite (all 18,538 states meet this by the verified integrity invariants)
4_safety_denominator.masked_states: none expected; any state with a missing or non-finite candidate label is excluded and counted separately. T90-reached states stay eligible (T90 is constant across their candidates).
4_safety_denominator.harm: state s is harmful iff key(selected(s), s) > key(d(s), s) under the frozen lexicographic order (one-step counterfactual from the same state)
4_safety_denominator.abstention_fallback: a recommendation of d(s) (abstention, fallback, or no switch) is counted in the denominator and is never harmful; a different candidate whose key equals d(s)'s is not harmful
4_safety_denominator.duplicates: the 298 candidate rows of a state never count as separate decisions; only the one selected recommendation is scored
4_safety_denominator.harm_rate: (# eligible states with harm) / (# eligible states in the family)
4_safety_denominator.criterion: upper bound of the two-sided 95% bootstrap CI (trajectory-clustered, 2,000 resamples, seed 5544103) <= 1%, in every test family
4_safety_denominator.minimum_sample_size: the >= 300 figure is a minimum requirement on the number of eligible states per test family for the safety criterion to be evaluable; it is not the denominator. Current eligible counts: TEST_PRIMARY_JOINT 3,256; TEST_HELDOUT_TIMING 1,841; TEST_HELDOUT_COMPLIANCE 2,989; DIAG_EXTRAPOLATION 1,442; DIAG_TEMPLATE_ZERO_SHOT 1,180 (all >= 300).
4_safety_denominator.secondary: number and share of deviating recommendations (selected != d(s)) and harm rate among deviating states

5_selector_semantics.original: selector_design.json step 1: 'Masking: skip T90 when T90_reached_before_decision; drop behaviorally duplicate candidates (keep lowest id).'
5_selector_semantics.problem: behavioral duplicates are determined by label maps that depend on hidden compliance and exit labels
5_selector_semantics.amended_step_1: Masking: skip T90 when T90 has been reached, decided observably as normalized_remaining <= 4/40 (i.e. at least 36 of 40 occupants evacuated). No candidate is removed.
5_selector_semantics.candidates: all 298 BASE2_298 candidates are scored independently from (26 features, candidate descriptor) and stay available
prohibited: removing candidates via hidden compliance, hidden exits, equivalence_class, realized outcomes
any use of simulator state beyond the 26 features
5_selector_semantics.ties: identical predictions tie naturally; after the frozen tolerance-lexicographic filtering and safety floor (selector_design.json steps 2-5, unchanged), the remaining tie is resolved deterministically: d(s) if it is in the final set, otherwise the lowest candidate id (ids frozen in candidate_action_set.json)
5_selector_semantics.observable_grouping: not used by the primary selector; any later optimization may use only observable candidate semantics (issue 2) and needs a separate approval

6_model_input_whitelist.whitelist_candidate_descriptor: 28 columns cand_<zone>_<value> for zone in (R1, R2, C1, R3, R4, C2, H) and value in (UNTOUCHED, FAVOR_A, PARITY, FAVOR_B), in that order, derived only from candidate_id via candidate_action_set.json
6_model_input_whitelist.exact_input: the 26 state features in the order above, followed by the 28 descriptor columns: 54 columns
6_model_input_whitelist.runtime_assertion: before every fit and every predict: assert list(model_input_columns) == WHITELIST (exact names and order), else raise; any extra, missing or reordered column aborts

preserved_limitations.A: 60% of decision states are at ticks 0 and 5 and fixed by the occupant layout (20 distinct inputs across 11,088 states).
preserved_limitations.B: G3 candidate sufficiency never tested beyond 4 non-empty eligible zones.
preserved_limitations.C: Diagnostic generalization family A (held-out seeds) requires the separately deferred Test A batch.
